subject: chemistry
title: Reversible reactions and dynamic equilibrium
key_idea: In a **reversible reaction** the products can react to make the original reactants. If it is exothermic in one direction it is endothermic in the other, with the same energy change. In a closed system it reaches **dynamic equilibrium** when the forward and reverse rates are equal.

blocks.text: Most reactions go one way. In a reversible reaction the products can react to make the reactants again.

items.meaning: A reaction in which the products can react to produce the original reactants.
The symbol for a reversible reaction. It has arrows in both directions.

blocks.label: A reversible reaction
where: the forward reaction makes C and D from A and B
the reverse reaction makes A and B from C and D

items: The direction of a reversible reaction can be changed by changing the conditions.
Heating and adding water are two ways to change the direction of the copper sulfate reaction below.

blocks.label: Hydrated and anhydrous copper sulfate
where: CuSO₄·5H₂O is hydrated copper sulfate, a blue solid
CuSO₄ is anhydrous copper sulfate, a white solid

rows: The solid turns white and steam (water vapour) is given off
Add water to the white solid

items: Adding water to white anhydrous copper sulfate is a test for water. The colour changes from white to blue.
When a hydrated solid is heated in an open tube, the mass decreases. Water vapour is made and escapes from the tube.
A reversible reaction can go in both directions, shown by ⇌.
Changing the conditions changes the direction.
Hydrated copper sulfate (blue) and anhydrous copper sulfate (white) is the standard example.

blocks.text: The energy change in the two directions is linked.

items: If the reaction is **exothermic** in one direction, it is **endothermic** in the opposite direction.
The **same amount of energy** is transferred in each direction.
In the copper sulfate example, the energy taken in on heating equals the energy released when water is added.
Exothermic one way means endothermic the other way.
The amount of energy is the same in both directions.

blocks.text: In a closed system a reversible reaction reaches a balance. This balance is called equilibrium.

items.meaning: Apparatus that stops reactants and products escaping, such as a sealed flask.
The state reached when the forward and reverse reactions occur at exactly the same rate.
Both the forward and reverse reactions are still happening.

items: A closed system is needed. If a product escapes, equilibrium cannot be reached.
At equilibrium the **rates** of the forward and reverse reactions are equal.
The **concentrations** of reactants and products stay constant. They are not necessarily equal.
The reactions have not stopped. They carry on at the same rate in both directions.

diagram.alt: A graph of the rate of the forward and reverse reactions against time. The forward rate starts high and falls. The reverse rate starts at zero and rises. They meet and stay level at equilibrium.
Put the steps by which a reversible reaction reaches equilibrium in order.
diagram.prompt: Put the steps to equilibrium in order
steps: The reactants are mixed in a closed system
The forward reaction is fastest and there is no reverse reaction yet
Products form and the reverse reaction starts
The forward rate falls and the reverse rate rises
The forward and reverse rates become equal
The concentrations stay constant: dynamic equilibrium

items: At equilibrium the forward and reverse rates are equal and the concentrations do not change.
It is dynamic: both reactions carry on.

checks.a: The reaction is reversible: the products can react to make the reactants again.

checks.q: Describe how a reversible reaction reaches equilibrium.
checks.a: It happens in a closed system, where reactants and products cannot escape. The forward and reverse reactions have the same rate.

checks.q: The forward reaction in a reversible reaction is exothermic. State whether the reverse reaction is exothermic or endothermic, and compare the energy changes.
checks.a: The reverse reaction is endothermic. The same amount of energy is transferred in each direction.

exam_phrases: the forward and reverse reactions have the same rate
in apparatus which prevents the escape of reactants and products
the forward and reverse reactions are taking place at (exactly) the same rate
the mass of each substance does not change
white to blue (anhydrous copper sulfate with water)
water vapour was produced; water (vapour) escaped

mistakes.wrong: The concentrations do not change at dynamic equilibrium because it is a closed system.
mistakes.right: A closed system is ignored in this answer. Say the forward and reverse reactions are taking place at exactly the same rate.

mistakes.wrong: When water is added to anhydrous copper sulfate the colour changes from blue to white.
mistakes.right: Anhydrous copper sulfate is white and hydrated is blue. The change is white to blue. Blue to white earns only 1 mark.

mistakes.wrong: The mass of the test tube decreased because the cobalt chloride reacted.
mistakes.right: Say that water vapour was produced and escaped from the tube, so its mass was not measured.

worked_example.question:
The reversible reaction for the production of ammonia is:

N₂(g) + 3H₂(g) ⇌ 2NH₃(g)

Describe how a reversible chemical reaction is able to reach equilibrium.
answer_points: The forward and reverse reactions have the same rate.
In apparatus which prevents the escape of reactants and products (a closed system).

exam_phrases: the solid goes white / steam is observed / water produced
add water / water rejoins / water reacts with the anhydrous solid
the solid goes blue (again) / heat is released
both forward and backward reactions take place at the same time
the rates of the two reactions are equal

mistakes.wrong: Put the copper sulfate in a closed system and explain the result using Le Chatelier's principle.
mistakes.right: Closed system and Le Chatelier are ignored here. Describe heating the crystals, the colour change, adding water, and the colour change back.

mistakes.wrong: When the blue crystals are heated they turn blue again.
mistakes.right: Heating hydrated copper sulfate gives a white solid, and steam or water is produced. The solid goes blue again when water is added.

worked_example.question:
Hydrated copper sulfate, CuSO₄·5H₂O, is a blue solid. Anhydrous copper sulfate, CuSO₄, is a white solid.

Heat energy is needed to convert hydrated copper sulfate to anhydrous copper sulfate. This is a reversible reaction.

CuSO₄·5H₂O ⇌ CuSO₄ + 5H₂O

Devise an experiment to show that this is a reversible reaction.
answer_points: The solid goes white, steam is seen, or water is produced.
Add water to the anhydrous solid (the water rejoins it).
The solid goes blue again, or heat is released.
worked_example.tip: The fourth mark does not depend on the third.

exam_phrases: the rates of the forward and backward reactions are equal
the forward and backward reactions still happen (so it is dynamic)
the concentrations of the reactants and products do not change
rate of forward reaction equals the rate of the backward reaction

mistakes.wrong: At dynamic equilibrium the concentrations of the reactants and products are the same.
mistakes.right: The same is not allowed. Say the concentrations of the reactants and products do not change.

mistakes.wrong: At dynamic equilibrium both reactions happen at a constant rate.
mistakes.right: Constant rate is ignored. Say the rates of the forward and backward reactions are equal.

worked_example.question:
Hydrogen gas is made by the reaction between methane, CH₄, and steam. The reaction reaches a dynamic equilibrium.

This is the equation for the reaction.

CH₄(g) + H₂O(g) ⇌ CO(g) + 3H₂(g)

State what is meant by a dynamic equilibrium.
answer_points: The rates of the forward and backward reactions are equal (so it is an equilibrium).
The forward and backward reactions still happen (so it is dynamic).
The concentrations of the reactants and products do not change.
worked_example.tip: Any two of the three statements score.
